summary: The triangle algebra is largely correct once a genuine bounded support triangle with three disjoint corner caps has been obtained. The reduction does not obtain such a triangle in all allowed configurations, and the treatment of parallel and limiting configurations contains false assertions and substantial equality gaps.
critical_errors: Three pairwise nonparallel supporting lines do not imply that their halfplanes containing Q' have bounded intersection. Their outward normals may lie in a semicircle, giving an unbounded intersection even though no two lines are parallel. The hypotheses do not exclude this, for example when one cap occupies a boundary chain whose total turning exceeds pi. Thus the claimed triangle P, its three labeled vertices, and all subsequent edge fractions need not exist. The proof treats only exact parallelism and omits this open class of unbounded support envelopes.

In the parallel case, the assertion that triangles obtained by moving the intersection to infinity have central and cap areas converging to those of Q' is false. A corner cap adjacent to the nearly parallel sides can have area tending to infinity, and even finite envelope caps generally converge to regions strictly larger than the original caps of Q'. Consequently the stated limit passage is not justified.
gaps: The identity P0=C0' is asserted from an informal same-sides description without proving that the three chosen support halfplanes together with the three H_i^- are an exact halfplane representation of C0'. This requires the correct cyclic adjacency and redundancy arguments, especially when a central chain has zero length. It also does not automatically persist after the support lines are perturbed in the parallel approximation.

The area formula |P0|=A(1-ac-be-df) requires the enlarged corner regions P_i to have pairwise disjoint interiors and to partition P with P0 up to boundaries. Disjointness of the original C_i does not by itself imply disjointness of the larger P_i; the needed implication from the ordering of the six edge intersections is not proved.

The limiting equality argument is incomplete. In the case c<=1/2, the displayed ratio bound forces only c to tend to 1/2, not a to tend to 1/2. Further control of the discarded slack is required. Even after convergence of all edge fractions were established, the proof gives no compactness argument showing that the support triangles remain bounded or that their limiting support lines form a medial triangle, particularly with fixed cutting lines and vertices escaping to infinity.
repair_hints: Provide a reduction that handles every possible orientation of the three central support halfplanes, including nonparallel unbounded intersections, rather than only bounded and exactly parallel cases.
Prove the exact six-halfplane representation of C0' and the corner-cap partition of a bounded support triangle before invoking the area identity.
Replace the parallel-limit assertions with a valid convergence and stability argument that tracks only quantities actually converging and rules out escaping vertices from all equality sequences.
